Buried in the rest of the news this week, I found the following interesting:

"NPR's Peter Overby reports that dozens of corporate sponsors have contributed
eight million dollars to help defray the cost of hosting the NATO summit. The
U.S. government is paying the rest of the bill -- 15 million dollars. The
companies have given cash, goods and services for the right to be called the
"NATO Host Committee." Critics say the U.S. is selling access to government
officials. "

http://www.npr.org/ramfiles/me/19990423.me.05.ram

"("We live in a world in which relatively few people - maybe 500 or 1,000 -
make the important decisions" - Philip B. Heymann of Harvard Law School, quoted
by Anthony Lewis, New York Times, April 21, 1995.)" Quoted by TK in para. 67 of
ISAIF.

I'm just waiting to see the commercials - "Official Sponsor of the NATO Summit"
or some such... $8million seems like such a drop in the bucket, compared to
talks of $10 billion or so as a proposed contribution to the NATO "action" in
Kosovo. I wonder whose great idea this was? Is it possible that campaign
finance reform is just getting to be a bit too popular of an issue? Is this a
sign of things to come, a way around what CFR is supposed to accomplish?

-Susan
